## Reading the index

Descriptions are the vendors' own, read from each `SKILL.md` frontmatter at the linked revision; only whitespace is normalized. Read the linked `SKILL.md` before choosing or running one: it owns the complete process, prerequisites and side effects. Source links point to the vendor commits checked out when this index was generated, so they work on GitHub as well as from a local Markdown viewer.

The four types are a navigation aid for this document. Guides come from a separate registry: the router consults them when selecting skills, and they are never workflow steps. Activities come from the catalog, which keeps the routing metadata; `scripts/list-skills` shows it next to the same descriptions.

The router itself is documented in [engineering-router](../skills/engineering-router/SKILL.md). Personal and project skills depend on local configuration and are not included in this shared vendor index. Inspect those with `scripts/list-skills --target <repo>`.

### Specification

Write down the expected behavior and boundaries.

| Skill | Description | Also applies to |
|---|---|---|
| [addyosmani/constraint-driven-development](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills/blob/301b02b12bff98e4688e6984af6556802322bbde/skills/constraint-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Establishes a project's quality bar as a written contract and stops agents quietly lowering it. Interviews the user on which dimensions matter, supplies sane default thresholds when they have no number in mind, records everything in CONSTRAINTS.md, and watches the diff for a weakened bar — new @ts-ignore or eslint-disable suppressions, skipped or deleted tests, assertions stripped out, unimplemented stubs, thresholds edited down. Use when no quality bar is written down, when the user says "set up constraints" or "define our standards", when the user wants dimensions they care about — accessibility, web performance, coverage — set up as enforced constraints, when an agent keeps silencing checks or skipping tests to get to green, when you need a coverage or performance threshold and don't know what number to pick, or when an agent writes more code than anyone will read. | Setup |

## Keeping the index current

After a reviewed catalog or vendor revision change, run `scripts/skill-index` and review the diff with the catalog change. `scripts/skill-index --check` reports a stale index; `scripts/selftest` runs it. `scripts/update` only reports upstream changes; review those before editing the catalog.
